# tagger

The goal of tagger is to easily add tags to facetted plots in order to
identify panles.

## Installation

You can install the development version from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("eliocamp/tagger")
```

## Example

In the default usage, you can simply add
[`tag_facets()`](https://eliocamp.github.io/tagger/reference/tag_facets.md)
to add a tag to each panel of a ggplo2 plot.

``` r

library(tagger)
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(hp, mpg)) +
   geom_point() +
   facet_grid(cyl ~ vs) +
   tag_facets()
```

![](reference/figures/README-example-1.png) If you want to tag rows and
columns instead of each panel indivdually, you can set it with the `tag`
argument.

``` r

ggplot(mtcars, aes(hp, mpg)) +
   geom_point() +
   facet_grid(cyl ~ vs) +
   tag_facets(tag = "rc")
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-2-1.png)

# Package index

## All functions

- [`get_layout()`](https://eliocamp.github.io/tagger/reference/get_layout.md)
  [`get_tag()`](https://eliocamp.github.io/tagger/reference/get_layout.md)
  [`get_row()`](https://eliocamp.github.io/tagger/reference/get_layout.md)
  [`get_col()`](https://eliocamp.github.io/tagger/reference/get_layout.md)
  : Get labels assigned to each panel of a tagged plot
- [`tag_facets()`](https://eliocamp.github.io/tagger/reference/tag_facets.md)
  : Adds tags to facets
